Jordan — thanks for the diagram and sheet. Quick notes after an initial scan: 

- Control-plane: We can terminate mTLS at the EdgeCloud edge LB and forward to the control-plane cluster using TLS passthrough. However, preserving source IP requires the LB to be configured in "proxy protocol v2" mode to the control-plane nodes. That is doable but depends on the customer's switch ACLs.
- Data-plane egress: The suggested hairpin path on page 2 will break when symmetric hashing is enabled on the leaf switch; we recommend keeping stateful proxies on the same L3 segment as the compute pods to avoid asymmetric flows.
- NAT: If Acme's colo does outbound NAT, we need an SNAT exemption for control-plane health checks so they don't appear as new tenants.

I attached a short firewall rule snapshot from our test cluster that shows the proxy-protocol config we usually apply.

Attachments: [attachment: edgecloud-proxyprotocol-example.txt (TXT, 3KB)]

Happy to join Wed 9/15 — 10am PT works for our ops lead.

—Steve

- Move stateful proxy pods to the same L3 segment as runtime nodes (see diagram layer A) to avoid asymmetric hashing issues.
- Add a health-check source IP whitelist to the control-plane to avoid SNAT conflicts.

Action items before Wed: 
- Karthik: can you call out the specific kernel/conntrack limits we'd need to raise for the proxy pattern? Put numbers in control-data-mapping.xlsx under "runtime_limits" tab.
- Kimberly: please draft a brief operational rollback step for an LB misconfig (one paragraph) and attach to runbook-draft.md.
- Naomi: add the evidence items we'll need for Acme's SOC/audit — token logging and retention windows.

I'll push v1.1 diagram and a lightweight agenda to the Drive link by EOD.
